I think early access is just a terrible idea as both a gamer and developer.

From a developer's perspective you stand to potentially ruin your product's reputation before it's even ready to be judged. As much as you may call something an alpha or a beta gamers are likely going to associate those terms with how they're used in console games or big PC releases. In that domain 'alpha' and 'beta' are increasingly often being used as marketing gimmicks. The company releases a time constrained demo of a release candidate a month or two before public release. If you have any complaints about the game? Don't worry, it's just a beta! Release an actual beta, let alone alpha, level product and watch your product's reputation get destroyed overnight as gamers complain it's filled with bugs or even things that are not entirely implemented yet. I'd never heard of this game, but checking out the forum it's nothing but people complaining about bugs. Shocker. In a highly competitive field you've just lost the interest of any consumer that might have been intrigued by your game and decided to go check out the forums before committing to a purchase.

Another issue is you blow your hype and release window. Your players either jump in early playing a buggy and nonrepresentative version of your game and then a year or two later you're trying to get people excited about a game that other people have already been playing (and probably complaining about) for years.

And finally you also destroy your own financial incentive for continued development. With much of your market having already purchased the game, your revenue stream will likely only decrease. If you've been irresponsible with the funding, as many amateur developers unsurprisingly are, then you can easily find yourself in a situation where you literally can no longer afford to work on your project and must either seek another round of funding, terminate full time work on the project, or at the minimum minimize the working team which has the same effect anyhow.
